newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs seen up cautiously, eyes on scam probe.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs seen up cautiously, eyes on scam probe.

text.p: Brazilian stock prices are seen rising cautiously Monday as investors keep their eyes on investigations into an alleged cash-for-votes scandal and await a U.S. FOMC meeting Tuesday, brokers said.
Traders said concerns eased after local newspapers and magazines over the weekend did not bring any further news on the alleged scam that could worry investors too much.

Traders apparently downplayed a report by Folha de Sao Paulo daily Sunday that there are more recordings of conversations between lawmakers and an unidentified speaker dubbed "Mr X" suggesting the alleged scam involves more legislators than those linked to the scheme so far.

They said it appears that the government will manage to prevent lawmakers from setting up a broad congressional inquiry into the case but noted investors would pay attention to any further developments of the alleged scandal.

Brazil's stock market was shaken last week by a series of reports by Folha citing taped conversations between lawmakers and "Mr X" which suggest that deputies took bribes to vote in favor of a re-election bill.
Analysts also said investors are awaiting Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve meeting in which another hike in U.S. interest rates could be decided.
